'''Bidiagonalization''' is one of unitary (orthogonal) [[matrix decomposition]]s such that '''U'''* '''A''' '''V''' = '''B''', where '''U''' and '''V''' are [[unitary matrix|unitary]] ([[orthogonal matrix|orthogonal]]) matrices; * denotes [[Hermitian transpose]]; and '''B''' is upper [[Bidiagonal matrix|bidiagonal]]. '''A''' is allowed to be rectangular.

For [[dense matrix|dense matrices]], the left and right unitary matrices are obtained by a series of [[Householder reflection]]s alternately applied from the left and right. This is known as Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization. For large matrices, they are calculated iteratively by using [[Lanczos algorithm|Lanczos method]], referred to as Golub-Kahan-Lanczos method.

Bidiagonalization has a very similar structure to the [[singular value decomposition]] (SVD). However, it is computed within finite operations, while SVD requires iterative schemes to find singular values. The latter is because the squared singular values are the roots of [[characteristic polynomial]]s of '''A'''* '''A''', where '''A''' is assumed to be tall.
